name: bootstrap_confidence_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Standard technical indicators provide point estimates (e.g., 'RSI is 28') without confidence intervals. Using block bootstrap resampling on rolling 1-min return data, we construct confidence intervals for the expected forward return. If the 90% bootstrap CI for the 30-bar forward return is entirely above zero, we have statistically robust evidence for a long entry. If entirely below zero, a short entry. When the CI straddles zero, no edge — stay flat. This eliminates entries where the point estimate looks good but uncertainty is too high. The inefficiency exists because bootstrap inference requires computational resources (1000 resamples per signal) and statistical knowledge beyond most market participants.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; at least 120 bars of session data for bootstrap base sample

indicators.name: Forward_Return_Proxy
indicators.params: mean(ROC(close,1), window=30) * 30 — estimated 30-bar forward return based on current regime

indicators.name: Block_Bootstrap_CI
indicators.params: 90% CI from 500 block bootstrap samples (block_size=5) of last 120 1-min returns, projected forward 30 bars

indicators.name: CI_Lower
indicators.params: 5th percentile of bootstrap distribution of 30-bar forward returns

indicators.name: Signal_Strength
indicators.params: min(abs(CI_Lower), abs(CI_Upper)) / CI_Width — how far the CI is from zero relative to its width

conditions: CI_Lower > 0 (entire 90% CI is above zero — high confidence in positive forward return)
CI_Lower > 5 bps (minimum expected return even at 5th percentile)
long.confirmation: ROC(close, 5) > 0 (recent momentum agrees with bootstrap prediction)

conditions: CI_Upper < 0 (entire 90% CI is below zero — high confidence in negative forward return)

exit.target: Forward_Return_Proxy bps from entry (estimated expected return)
exit.stop_loss: abs(CI_Lower) bps for longs / abs(CI_Upper) bps for shorts (bootstrap worst case)
exit.trailing_stop: After CI_median profit, trail at CI_Width * 0.3 from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: CI shifts to include zero (confidence in direction lost)

risk.position_sizing: Scale with Signal_Strength: ₹75K if strength 0-0.3, ₹1L if 0.3-0.6, ₹1.25L if > 0.6

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; high VIX widens CIs, making it harder to get directional signals
filters.time_filter: No entries before 11:15 (need 120 bars for bootstrap base sample) or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: None — bootstrap CI inherently captures trend information
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day — bootstrap from non-event data doesn't represent event-day distributions
other_filters: CI_Width must be < 50 bps (uncertainty not too high — otherwise even 'directional' CIs are too wide to be meaningful)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — bootstrap inference for trading signals is novel; the computational requirement (500 resamples per signal evaluation) provides a natural barrier to replication

weaknesses: Block bootstrap with block_size=5 assumes serial dependence structure decays within 5 bars — if the true dependence is longer (e.g., 15-bar cycles), the bootstrap CIs are invalid
Computing 500 bootstrap resamples per signal evaluation per stock adds significant latency — may not complete within the 1-minute bar window for real-time trading across 50 stocks
The 'CI entirely above/below zero' requirement is very restrictive — in noisy 1-min data, bootstrap CIs tend to be wide and straddle zero most of the time, generating very few signals
prior_art: Efron (1979) bootstrap; Politis & Romano (1994) block bootstrap for time series; White (2000) reality check bootstrap for trading strategies; application to real-time entry signals is novel
notes: Consider using the stationary bootstrap (Politis & Romano 1994) with random block lengths instead of fixed block_size=5 for more robust inference. Pre-compute the bootstrap on a slightly lagged window (120 bars ending 5 bars ago) to reduce latency impact. NumPy vectorization can speed up the 500 resamples to under 50ms.
